criteria.criterion: After `heal_multi_bundle` on a ref with two divergent bundles, exactly one bundle remains, a fresh clone succeeds, and every unique commit from both heads is reachable from the healed tip. Verified by the real-git-repo oracle.

The heal never discards a head/event: a commit unique to the non-chosen head is present in the healed history (the specific regression upstream's interactive doctor causes). Verified by the reachability assertion.

The heal writes the merged tip before deleting any original bundle and never deletes the merged tip, so at every crash point ≥1 bundle carrying the full merged history remains remotely; a mid-delete crash re-heals to a single lossless bundle on the next run. Verified by the crash-recovery oracle.

On an unexpected non-derived-file conflict the heal aborts without deleting any remote bundle, releases the lock, and surfaces `rebar fsck-recover` — no parent dropped. Verified by the conflict-path oracle.

Concurrent doctors do not corrupt or duplicate-repair: with N processes behind a barrier, exactly one merges (the rest observe the helper's held per-ref lock and back off without healing), and the final shared remote is a single healed bundle with full reachability. Verified by the multi-process race oracle.
`push_tickets_branch` auto-invokes the heal on the multi-bundle signature exactly once and the push converges afterward (no infinite non-FF retry loop). Verified by the push-path test.

The doctor's local merge runs under rebar's `write_lock` and cannot race a concurrent local committer (HEAD/index are never mutated outside the lock); the helper's S3 ref-lock is the outer lock and `write_lock` the inner, a fixed cycle-free order. Verified by the local-lock serialization oracle.

The doctor folds N heads via **iterated 2-parent merges** (not an octopus merge), following `sync`'s existing lossless-merge semantics, and `sync`'s `reconverge`/`_union_merge` keep identical observable behavior. Verified by the existing sync suite plus the N≥3-head fold oracle asserting all heads reachable.

A fetched bundle head that shares no common ancestor with HEAD is handled explicitly: the fold still unions it via `--allow-unrelated-histories`. The abort/refuse path fires only when `git merge` reports a genuine content conflict. Verified by two oracles — an unrelated-history union oracle and a content-conflict abort oracle.

The heal keeps append-only semantics and adds **no** direct S3 SDK dependency to core rebar: all S3 access (lock, enumerate, put, delete, HEAD) is via git-remote-s3's own `S3Remote`/`.s3` imported lazily behind `require_s3_helper()`; no `merge=union` driver is used; the helper lock TTL is unchanged (default 60s). Verified by inspection and by rebar importing with the `[s3]` extra absent.
